preceding_text: 1 Registration and sign in
Signed in account: Not signed in
Page shown: Registration

A new applicant or provider starts at registration, selects the appropriate account type and supplies the requested identity and contact information. Follow the email verification instructions before continuing. An existing demo account instead signs in using its username or email. The middle initial is optional.
2 Applicant profile and supporting evidence
Signed in account: learner.aurora
Page shown: Applicant profile

The applicant maintains identity, contact, education, household, and location details. Section edit modals keep the applicant on their record. Upload documents that support the profile rather than merely filling the text fields.

figures.subsection: Open the applicant verification record
preceding_text: 1. Select Applicant Verification from Applicant verification. Confirm the name and account before reviewing.
2. Read the review guide for the current step. Expand the complete profile only when more context is needed, and check any changes since the previous decision.
3. Go to Supporting evidence and compare each required document with the corresponding declared information.
4. Uploaded files do not verify the whole profile. Review current evidence first; use the queue navigation to keep the original search and filters while opening the next record.
4 Provider organization profile
Signed in account: orivanta.profile
Page shown: Provider profile

The organization profile manager maintains the provider information shown to applicants, including identity, public description, branding, contact information, and location. A provider preview shows the applicant-facing presentation.

figures.subsection: Review organization documents individually
preceding_text: 1. Sign in as lumenops.reviews, open Provider verification and select Orivanta Learning Foundation. Read its saved approval and individual proof history. To demonstrate a fresh review, first deliberately reopen the appropriate review or replace evidence through its actual workflow; do this only after the operational demonstration if it would block provider access.

2. Choose Review on one file. Compare the submitted proof with the legal organization name, registration authority and number, and representative details. Download it if the format cannot be previewed.

3. Choose Accept document only after inspecting it and checking the comparison acknowledgement. Otherwise choose Request replacement and explain what must be corrected. Saving records the reviewer, time, note and file revision; it does not verify the account.

4. In a fresh review, repeat for each current file. Unreviewed, unavailable and replacement-requested evidence blocks approval. Reload if another reviewer or upload changes the record. Do not resave an existing approval merely to make a demonstration look complete.
6 Program creation and publication
Signed in account: orivanta.programs
Page shown: Provider program review

Use orivanta.programs with the draft Orivanta Digital Learning Grant. Complete Basics, Support, Schedule, Eligibility, Application and Selection, then inspect the actual values in Review. Saving a draft is private; submitting sends the program to admin publication review. Orivanta College Pathways Award is already awaiting that review.

figures.subsection: Inspect the submitted scholarship before publication
preceding_text: 1. Open a program from Program review and confirm its provider and submission status.
2. Review the advertised support, eligibility, requirements, dates, selection process and recipient terms.
3. Read the readiness checks and changes since the previous review, then approve a valid submission or request clear changes with a review note.
4. Save only after checking the current submission. If another user changed it, reload before deciding. Publication is separate from selecting a scholarship applicant.
8 Scholarship discovery and preparation
Signed in account: learner.aurora
Page shown: Applicant scholarships

Use Search and filter to find published scholarships, then open View details to review benefits, eligibility, required files, deadlines and application instructions. Each result displays the scholarship logo beside its name; background photographs and provider logos are separate assets. Apply starts the application only when the verified profile meets the required rules and applications are open. Use the provider link to inspect the organization.
9 Reusable applicant documents
Signed in account: learner.aurora
Page shown: Applicant documents

My Documents holds reusable files for future applications. A saved document is not automatically an accepted application requirement; the applicant must choose appropriate current files during an application.
10 Submitted application and next action
Signed in account: learner.aurora
Page shown: Applicant application
The application details tell the applicant the current stage, what happens next, required submissions, schedule, decision, and history. learner.aurora is waiting for the initial provider review.

figures.subsection: Inspect application eligibility after selecting an applicant
preceding_text: 1. Open Applicant Aurora from My review queue and confirm that the application is assigned to you.
2. Compare the declared profile against each program rule. Review unresolved items rather than relying only on an overall score.
3. Inspect the Profile tab and supporting evidence where a claim needs checking.
4. Hard requirements and reviewable qualifications must follow their configured policy; resolve the relevant review before recording a screening result.

figures.subsection: Review the application evidence
preceding_text: 1. Open Evidence in the selected application record.
2. Use View or the file preview to inspect the submitted file, then select Review beside that document.
3. Record an evidence status and specific review notes appropriate to the file. An upload alone is not accepted evidence.
4. Repeat for the required files before relying on document readiness for the screening result.
12 Formal application verification
Signed in account: orivanta.selection
Page shown: Provider formal

Formal application is a configured stage for providers that require a further official application or in-person verification. Applicants follow the published instructions and schedule where applicable. A separate session is not always mandatory for this stage.
13 Examination and interview scheduling
Signed in account: orivanta.selection
Page shown: Provider sessions

The selection officer assigns eligible applicants to sessions. Separate sessions support different dates or venues; online interviews use a meeting link. Session attendance or completion and an individual applicant result are different records.
14 Applicant examination schedule
Signed in account: learner.cielo
Page shown: Applicant exam

The applicant reads the assigned examination date, venue, instructions, and acknowledgement action. Other prepared accounts cover completing the conducted session and recording an individual examination result.
15 Applicant interview schedule
Signed in account: learner.brio
Page shown: Applicant interview
The interview schedule tells the applicant when and how to attend, including the meeting link for an online interview. An applicant acknowledgement does not prove the interview took place.
16 Recording conducted stage results
Signed in account: orivanta.selection
Page shown: Provider interview result

The results workspace separates work ready for result recording from scheduling work. Complete the required conducted-session or stage verification and attach proof where required before recording an applicant result.

figures.subsection: Open the final decision form
preceding_text: 1. As orivanta.decisions, open Pending decisions, choose Orivanta Academic Merit Scholarship and open Applicant Aurora. Read the saved evaluations, capacity and provisional comparison reason. Applicant Dune is in this same intake, not a second scoring scholarship.

2. The current three totals are 95.5, 90.6 and 85.0; Dune has no final score. Because a pending evaluation is missing, do not describe the comparison as Ready to compare. Complete the missing assessment in the selection workspace, then reload and use the actual revised cohort order.

3. In Record final outcome, choose the actual decision and add the required notes or internal rationale. A different suggestion or a cutoff tie can require an explanation. A waitlist suggestion is not an official waitlist entry until saved.

4. Review the confirmation and save only the intended outcome. If another decision or score changed, reload the comparison. Selection reserves capacity and sends the offer; it does not accept the agreement for the applicant or release money.

figures.subsection: Compare final candidates using the DSS
preceding_text: 2. Inspect the actual four-candidate scores, ranks, ties and two remaining slots. Dune enters the order using the score the tester records, so do not assume the first two prepared rows will remain the highest. Suggestions are advisory and are not official outcomes.
3. Open the small evaluation-breakdown icon. Compare frozen screening, examination and interview components and their weights. These are recorded evaluations, not the applicant matching percentage.
4. Open Record decision for the intended candidate. Follow the result controls and confirmation. Enter a clear internal reason if departing from guidance or resolving a cutoff tie.
5. Return to Pending decisions after saving. Capacity and suggestions update. Equal scores can share a rank; an unresolved tie at the cutoff must not be arbitrarily treated as an automatic winner.

figures.subsection: Read the scored stage breakdown
preceding_text: 1. Open the evaluation-breakdown icon for Applicant Aurora.
2. Read the stage status, score, maximum and weight. Screening reuses the reviewed academic-merit and financial-need rubric components.
3. Treat formal verification as a prerequisite. It is not counted twice as additional points.
4. If a stage is incomplete or its result was reopened, review it through the responsible workspace before relying on the final total.

figures.subsection: Complete a missing evaluation before ranking
preceding_text: 1. As orivanta.selection, open the completed interview through selection history, then the assigned applicant record. Confirm participation and the original assessment evidence.

2. Expand Earlier stage evaluations in the applicant record. Beside Interview, choose Add score and enter the actual score and maximum. Add a factual note and review the confirmation before recording it.
3. To correct an existing evaluation later, use the correction control and give the required explanation. Earlier score revisions stay in history.
4. As orivanta.decisions, select this program in Pending decisions. A final score appears only after all scored and qualifying prerequisites are complete. Missing does not mean zero.

figures.subsection: Read and respond to the recipient agreement
preceding_text: 2. Read the actual recipient terms, responsibilities and any stated consequences rather than accepting from the summary alone.
3. Use the acceptance acknowledgement and response note where required, then choose the intended response.
4. Only submit after understanding the agreement. The provider must wait for the applicant response before the corresponding support steps.
5. If the agreement is already accepted, View agreement shows the saved terms. Use a still-pending offer to demonstrate acceptance; do not reset an existing response.
19 Recipient support and agreement tracking
Signed in account: orivanta.recipients
Page shown: Recipient closeout

Use orivanta.recipients to inspect Applicant Brio in Orivanta Term Assistance Grant. The agreement is accepted and its original-document check is closed. The support-status record is ready for a deliberate renewal or completion decision; agreement concerns and withdrawal branches are separate and are not pre-recorded.

figures.section: 20 Applicant scholarship support and in person check in
figures.subsection: Open the appointment and prepare the originals
preceding_text: 1. Open Orivanta Term Assistance Grant, then Check-ins and the upcoming appointment. Read its date, time, exact venue, map pin and the original records requested.
2. Open the upcoming appointment and read the Manila date, time, venue, and instructions.
3. Bring the current academic record and enrollment certificate. This record has no applicant upload form.

4. Use View map for the venue and follow the appointment instructions. Contact the provider for a different schedule; do not upload substitute files for this in-person check. Return after attendance for the provider-recorded results.

figures.subsection: Select a recipient and open the monitoring checklist
preceding_text: 1. As orivanta.monitoring, open Orivanta Continuing Learners Grant and select Applicant Cielo in the attended check-in. Attendance is recorded; current academic and enrollment results still need the provider review.
2. Select Applicant Cielo from the roster. Attendance is already recorded; the two original documents still need provider results.

3. Open Current academic record. Compare the original, enter the verified grade and grading scale, select the result and record notes. Repeat for Current enrollment certificate. These are provider records, not applicant uploads.
4. Switch to Applicant Dune to demonstrate Close check-in after both items are met. Review the closure dialog and confirm the case outcome. Closing one check-in does not renew or end the scholarship.

figures.subsection: Set up and activate the monitoring plan
preceding_text: 2. In Requirements, add only necessary academic, enrollment or other program checks. For academic progress, choose the required minimum and grading scale.
3. Configure the actual evidence method. The demonstrated check-ins require the provider to inspect originals at an appointment, not accept an applicant upload as verified proof.
4. Open Review and compare all settings with the published support terms. Save draft while preparing; activate only the intended complete plan after confirmation.
5. Use orivanta.monitoring to publish individual appointments from the active plan. Activating a plan does not by itself assign every recipient to a new appointment.

figures.subsection: Publish a check in for the selected recipients
preceding_text: 2. Name the period, academic year and appointment. Set the actual date, time, venue, original documents to bring and short recipient instructions.
3. Choose the intended accepted recipients from the roster. Keep separate sessions or recipient arrangements for different dates and venues instead of publishing overlapping appointments.
4. Review the recipient count and instructions, then confirm Publish check-in only when ready. Cancel leaves the current data unchanged.
5. Sign in as an assigned applicant and open Scholarship Support then Check-ins. Confirm that the appointment and required originals appear for that applicant.

figures.subsection: Record attendance originals and case closure
preceding_text: 1. For a new actual appointment, record Attended only after the applicant attends. If the appointment changes, use the reschedule controls and notify the recipient instead of pretending the old meeting occurred.

2. Review Applicant Cielo in Continuing Learners Grant. Open Current academic record, inspect the physical original, and record the verified grade, scale, result and notes. Repeat for enrollment. Applicant Dune in this same grant has both required items met and can demonstrate Close check-in.

3. If an extension, exception or follow-up is genuinely needed, record it through the available request or follow-up controls and resolve it before normal closure. Do not mark a pending item met to remove the blocker.
4. Select Applicant Dune. Both items are already met. Choose Close check-in, review the outcome and confirm it. The applicant can then read the closed result.
22 Admin monitoring oversight
Signed in account: lumenops.reviews
Page shown: Admin monitoring
The review officer can inspect monitoring records and supporting evidence through its own oversight workspace. This is separate from routine provider checklist review.
23 Renewal completion and support decisions
Signed in account: orivanta.recipients
Page shown: Recipient closeout

Open Applicant Brio, learner.brio, in Orivanta Term Assistance Grant as orivanta.recipients, then Support status. Its check-in is closed and both allowance and school-supplies receipts are confirmed. Renew support if the award continues, or complete support when the agreed obligations are finished. The current support decision is deliberately left to the tester. Outstanding schedules, unconfirmed receipts and unresolved delivery issues block normal completion.

figures.subsection: Read the applicant closeout summary
preceding_text: In practice, the award terms determine whether support ends at graduation, at the end of a term, or through an early decision. A period ending without renewal is not the same as ending it early. Some programs require final documents before the last release. See UP Diliman DOST-ASTHRDP procedures and CHED Merit Scholarship guidelines on notice and appeal.
Read the applicant closeout summary
Signed in account: learner.brio

The screenshot shows learner.brio in the Term Assistance Grant support history before a current renewal or completion has been saved. There is no separate pre-renewed applicant. First record the intended eligible support decision as orivanta.recipients, then return with this same applicant to inspect its saved reason, effective date and available response. Completed support moves to Past support only after completion.

figures.subsection: Renew support and read the recipient response
preceding_text: 1. Open Applicant Brio in Term Assistance Grant and inspect Support status. Check the closed document review, accepted agreement and settled cash and school-supplies benefits. Choose Renewed only when the provider intends to continue support.
2. Record a matching reason category, effective date, renewed support end, next review and the next-period terms. Review the confirmation before saving.

3. Sign in as the recipient. Open Support history and the renewal outcome, then read its dates, reasons and terms. Use the acknowledgment or permitted response rather than accepting a different current program page.
4. Do not look for a separate successful-renewal account. The response becomes available on learner.brio after this actual provider decision. Refresh the history if another tab was already open.

figures.section: 24 Planning the first or one time benefit release
preceding_text: 24 Planning the first or one time benefit release
Signed in account: orivanta.releases
Page shown: Provider release schedule

The benefit release officer can schedule the first distribution after the required agreement state without creating recurring monitoring merely to distribute a benefit. One-time awards can use no recurring monitoring policy.

figures.subsection: Open the distribution record and record delivery
preceding_text: 1. Select the relevant release from Record distribution and confirm the title, schedule and recipients.
2. Select the intended recipient and inspect the current distribution status before entering a result.
3. Record actual delivery details and attach required proof. Do not mark a scheduled event as delivered merely because its date arrived.
4. The applicant must still confirm receipt or report an issue. Provider evidence alone cannot make that response for the applicant.

figures.subsection: Submit payout details for a digital benefit
preceding_text: Signed in account: learner.dune

Use a newly scheduled bank or e-wallet release that actually requests destination details to demonstrate entering them. The prepared learner.dune Term Assistance Grant record has already submitted its fictional e-wallet destination, so its current screen demonstrates the submitted status rather than an empty entry form. The provider must review it next.
2. Choose Add payout details. Enter the institution, account holder, and the fictional account number for the release method.
3. Review and submit. The provider must review the destination; saving the details does not send money.

figures.subsection: Review the payout destination
preceding_text: Signed in account: orivanta.releases

Use the scheduled Term Assistance Grant release for Applicant Dune. Its e-wallet details are submitted and still await provider review. Compare only the information necessary to confirm the destination; request a correction with a specific reason when it cannot be confirmed.
2. Inspect the submitted details. Approve a matching destination or request a correction from the applicant.
3. Approval unlocks recording a transfer. It does not send the benefit and does not confirm receipt.

figures.subsection: Record simulated transfer proof
preceding_text: Signed in account: orivanta.releases

For this same Applicant Dune release, finish the payout destination review first. The reset does not include a separate pre-approved bank transfer. Only after approval should the release officer record the actual simulated transfer date, reference and required provider proof. The platform records the evidence; it does not send bank money itself.
2. For the demo, record a simulated transfer date and attach fictional proof. Do not send real money. In actual use, record a transfer only after completing it outside the portal.
3. Confirm the record. The applicant can then acknowledge receipt or report a problem.

figures.subsection: Follow up a missed benefit release
preceding_text: 1. Open the distribution, select the recipient, and record the missed release only if the scheduled delivery did not happen. Find it again under Issues & follow-up.

2. Send a follow-up notice with instructions and at least seven days to reply. Allow at least two days between contact attempts. The reminder must leave at least two more days to reply and cannot shorten the original deadline.

3. The recipient can ask for a new arrangement or explicitly decline the benefit. Keep the missed attempt in history and link a replacement release when applicable. An actual reply stops closure for no response.

The reset does not pre-record a missed collection. learner.brio in Orivanta School Essentials Award has an upcoming collection appointment. Create a missed-release branch only after the scheduled time and actual non-attendance, then follow the required notice, reminder and response periods. Do not backdate contact or change the clock to unlock a shortcut.

figures.subsection: Reply to an uncollected benefit notice
preceding_text: 1. Once a follow-up notice actually exists, sign in as the applicant, open the award, Benefit releases and the release follow-up. Read the instructions and response deadline.

2. Choose the available response to request a new arrangement if the applicant still wants the benefit, or explicitly decline it only if that is the intended decision. Explain the circumstances and confirm.
3. As orivanta.releases, open the same missed release. Read the actual recipient response. For continued collection, schedule and link an eligible replacement for the same person and benefit.
4. Keep the missed attempt and notice in history. Record actual replacement delivery and obtain recipient receipt confirmation; do not label the missed original as received.

figures.subsection: Open a benefit record before confirming receipt
preceding_text: 1. Open the relevant benefit record rather than confirming from the list alone.
2. Read the recorded distribution details, benefit amount or description, and any available proof.
3. Confirm receipt only if you actually received the stated benefit. If it is missing or incomplete, use the delivery-issue response.
4. When a response is already recorded, inspect its status and history instead of sending a duplicate confirmation.

figures.subsection: Complete a one time award without recurring monitoring
preceding_text: 2. Confirm only the benefit actually received. If something is missing, submit the appropriate issue instead; a provider cannot confirm it for the applicant.
3. As orivanta.recipients, select Applicant Dune and open Support status. Before completing support shows the agreed one-time benefit settled with no outstanding distribution or delivery issue.
4. Choose Complete support with the accurate completion reason and effective date, then review and confirm. Do not create an unnecessary semester plan or grade check for this one-time award.
5. As Applicant Dune afterward, open Past support and the outcome to read the saved completion reason, dates, benefit summary and any permitted response.
27 Recipient withdrawal requests
Signed in account: orivanta.recipients
Page shown: Recipient withdrawals

An accepted recipient can request withdrawal with an explanation. Support does not end while the request is pending. A missed pickup or silence is not a withdrawal request. This process is separate from withdrawing an application before accepting an award.
28 Agreement concerns before conclusions
Signed in account: orivanta.recipients
Page shown: Recipient concerns

Agreement concerns begin as private drafts with a specific accepted obligation, factual explanation and proof. Sending the notice gives the applicant an opportunity to respond; a notice is not a confirmed breach. The live queue starts empty until a tester creates a case.
29 Provider delivery investigation and correction
Signed in account: orivanta.releases
Page shown: Provider delivery reports

The release officer responds to missing-benefit reports, requests information or proposes a documented delivery correction. The report stays unresolved until the applicant confirms receipt or gives the appropriate response.
30 Independent review appeals and privacy
Signed in account: lumenops.reviews
Page shown: Admin case review

The admin reviewer examines the accepted obligation or benefit, evidence, statements and response opportunity, then records a reasoned outcome. A different authorized reviewer must decide an appeal of the first reviewers outcome. Privacy and access details are collapsed inside an opened case.
31 Provider support and platform reports
Signed in account: orivanta.support
Page shown: Provider support

Provider support staff handle questions and track replies within their organization. Platform problems and privacy requests can be escalated through the platform support process rather than changing an applicant decision informally.
32 Admin support case handling
Signed in account: lumenops.support
Page shown: Admin support

The Support Officer owns the final platform reply. For a sign-in, password, email or account restriction issue, it can send a limited access task to the Account Manager. The original report and attachments stay with Support. A reply is not profile verification or a scholarship decision.
33 Provider staff and program assignment
Signed in account: orivanta.team
Page shown: Provider team

The team administrator manages staff access, role responsibilities and assigned scholarships. Limited program assignment prevents a staff member from automatically working on every program. Newly invited staff complete their first-login setup.

figures.subsection: Inspect and manage the selected account
preceding_text: 1. Open the account directory and select Applicant Aurora, learner.aurora, to inspect the current account controls. There is no pre-created support referral in this dataset. To demonstrate Return result, first create a justified access request and send it from lumenops.support, then open that task here.
2. Read the task, then inspect the relevant sign-in, verification-email, password or restriction controls. Use a separate access action only when it is actually required.

3. Select Return result, explain the checked account controls and any account-holder step, then confirm. The task returns to Support. No password reset, suspension or verification change is required merely to demonstrate this task.

4. Returning a result does not automatically change account access, verify the profile or close the support case. Support reviews the result and sends the final reply. A stale or already completed task cannot be saved twice.
35 Provider paid services and requests
Signed in account: orivanta.billing
Page shown: Provider billing

The provider billing role reviews available platform services, submits intake information, follows checkout and tracks delivery, files, meetings and acceptance. These are provider-to-platform services, not scholarship payments to applicants.

figures.section: 36 Admin service intake delivery and closeout
preceding_text: 36 Admin service intake delivery and closeout
Signed in account: lumenops.billing
Page shown: Admin billing

The Billing Officer handles intake, assignment, service delivery, files, meetings and closeout. Its Finance follow-up queue also contains internal payment-record questions, including questions about already closed services. Delivery, payment and refund states remain separate.
37 Admin finance and payment records
Signed in account: lumenops.finance
Page shown: Admin finance

The Finance Officer reviews confirmed payments, receipts and exceptions. An internal financial check can be sent to Billing and returned to Finance without changing the underlying transaction. Gateway confirmation, delivery completion and external refunds have their own states.

figures.subsection: Demonstrate the two admin handoffs from end to end
preceding_text: 2. Return to that same case as lumenops.support. Read the Account Manager finding and record the reporter-facing response. There is no separate account or seeded returned case for this step.

3. For Finance clarification, open a current paid service as lumenops.finance, use Request a Billing record check and confirm the precise question. Switch to lumenops.billing and respond in the same service record.

4. Reopen the same service as lumenops.finance, inspect the Billing response, then record the financial check and its finding. The prepared payment remains separate from the operational delivery status.

5. Use lumenops.records to follow the related service or support history afterward. Neither internal task completion sends money, closes the service automatically, verifies a profile or changes scholarship support.
38 Admin audit history and exports
Signed in account: lumenops.records
Page shown: Admin records

The Records Officer can follow exact related account, application, program, service or support records from an audit entry. The saved entry describes the event at that time; later events can supersede its outcome. Private handoff instructions and financial notes are not copied into audit metadata.

figures.section: 39 Provider manager overview and combined workspaces
preceding_text: 39 Provider manager overview and combined workspaces
Signed in account: orivanta.manager
Page shown: Provider manager

The provider manager has a cross-workspace overview for its organization rather than a separate new scholarship process. It can move between permitted programs, reviews, selection, decisions, recipients, monitoring and releases. Program assignment and organization boundaries still apply.
40 Organization representative view
Signed in account: orivanta
Page shown: Provider representative

The organization representative is the organization owner account. Its visible navigation and actions follow the current role model; do not assume it is interchangeable with every specialist or the provider manager. Use the named operational account for the process being demonstrated.
41 Portal manager overview
Signed in account: lumenops.manager
Page shown: Admin manager

The Portal Manager has read-only oversight across admin service areas. Team action counts show work currently owned by staff. Waiting steps show another team, the account holder or gateway; failed sign-in history is reference information, not automatically unresolved work. Totals count work items, not unique people.

figures.subsection: Open an admin team account in governance
preceding_text: 1. Review role coverage and any area with open work but no available owner. Select its role-coverage link to open the filtered admin team list.
2. Inspect the staff member and readiness label, such as email verification needed, password reset required, missing role permissions or access suspended.
3. Make only the intended governance change after its confirmation. Restoring readiness does not complete the operational work or grant unrelated permissions.
4. Return to the specialist queue with its assigned account. Demonstrate manager oversight and superadmin governance last, after the actual operational handoffs.
